provider.notes: Registered as `groq` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1705); live sessions build it through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:429). Groq has no streaming speech-to-text interface: both models are served by one synchronous multipart endpoint that is wire-compatible with OpenAI's. The existing client buffers audio and uploads only at hang-up, when the buffer reaches 20 MB, or when the client ends its audio by hand (an audio_end message on /ws, or a buffer commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), because the default flush strategy is OnDisconnect and no configuration path sets another (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/config.rs:521; client.rs:873-902), so a normal live call produces no transcript while it is in progress. Either act makes the voice manager disconnect and reconnect the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:301-322, also called from gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:1353-1354; gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672), and the disconnect uploads the buffer (client.rs:1085-1108). A push-to-talk client that ends each utterance itself is therefore the one kind of session that gets usable text from this provider during a call today. The same disconnect clears the result callback (client.rs:1114-1115) and nothing registers it again, so a second such act in the same session probably delivers nothing (inferred from reading, not run). An empty model resolves to whisper-large-v3-turbo (config.rs:47, :540-543). The client reads underscores as hyphens before it matches its short aliases (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/config.rs:126), so large_v3 also selects whisper-large-v3; the rows list only the hyphen spellings as model_aliases. There is no model allow-list: unknown ids are sent verbatim, and plugin metadata still advertises the retired distil-whisper-large-v3-en (mod.rs:146).

transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls (segmented_openai_compat) is not built yet. Today the Groq client buffers the caller audio and uploads it only at hang-up, when the client ends its audio by hand (audio_end, or a commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), or when its 20 MB buffer cap is reached, so a normal call gets no transcript while it is in progress.

measurements.conditions: Pipecat constant GROQ_TTFS_P99 = 1.54 s: end of speech to final transcript for its voice-activity-segmented Groq service, including a 200 ms detector stop delay. The Pipecat benchmark harness builds that service with whisper-large-v3-turbo (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipecat-ai/stt-benchmark/main/src/stt_benchmark/services.py, reported by the real-time levers research). The constant has not changed since 2026-02-09. No median is published; Groq itself publishes only a speed factor (216 times real time).

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request code lives inside the buffering client: send_request takes &mut self and writes rate-limit state and the last request id, so two uploads cannot be in flight; it is awaited on the audio path under the voice manager's speech-to-text write lock (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:636-639) behind a 120 s request timeout, a 30 s connect timeout and a three-attempt loop (client.rs:57, :60, :66). The loop retries network errors and timeouts; a typed 429 or 5xx reply is probably returned on the first attempt, because the retry test looks for the status digits or a lower-case 'rate limit' in a message that holds neither unless the vendor's error body failed to parse (client.rs:640-653, :806-825; inferred from reading, not run). The worst stall on the audio path is therefore three 120 s timeouts plus back-off, and a rate-limit reply probably fails the upload at once instead of waiting. The WAV is written at the session sample rate and channel count (client.rs:520-522), not 16 kHz mono. Groq speaks the OpenAI multipart request, so the shared OpenAI-compatible transcriber serves it with base URL https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (config.rs:35). The client keeps only the text and a derived confidence (client.rs:591-596); no_speech_prob and compression_ratio are parsed and dropped, and an empty transcript still fires the result callback. Ask for the `segment` timestamp granularity: `word` alone returns only word, start and end, without the quality fields. The prompt is limited to 224 tokens (config.rs:50). Take the language hint from the provider-mapped value: on the /ws path the configured language is mapped to ISO 639-1, with `auto` omitted, before the client is built (gateway/src/handlers/ws/config.rs:475-504; gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:239-242), while the DAG node passes its own default en-US unmapped (gateway/src/dag/nodes/provider.rs:334-343).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. The existing client allows 120 s per request, 30 s to connect and up to three attempts on network errors and timeouts (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/client.rs:57, :60, :66); the vendor audit recommends 5 s in total with one retry at most, roughly three times the third-party P99 of 1.54 s. It is an estimate to be replaced by the gateway's own measurement. Container (16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV: Groq downsamples to 16 kHz mono and says WAV gives lower latency), pre-roll, trailing silence, the 25 s maximum segment and two uploads in flight keep the defaults. Segments are still uploaded at each pause: the 10 s minimum billed per request costs about $0.0001 (turbo) or $0.0003 (large-v3), too little to justify holding a segment back. The binding constraint is the per-organisation request limit, so a deployment on the free plan (20 requests per minute) may choose upload_policy per_turn.

provenance.notes: The gateway's default Groq model (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/config.rs:47). File endpoint only: Groq has no stream parameter and no realtime or WebSocket audio endpoint. An asynchronous Batch API also accepts transcriptions, but it answers in 24 hours to 7 days, so it is not listed as a transport. max_upload_bytes is the 25 MB attachment limit, which is also the free-plan file limit; the Developer plan allows 100 MB files, and anything above the attachment limit goes through the `url` parameter. Groq's x-ratelimit request headers always describe the per-day request window, not the per-minute one, and its token headers describe tokens per minute, which do not limit audio; the limiter may read retry-after directly but must not take the request headers as the per-minute budget.

provenance.notes: Retired model kept in the map so that a session naming it gets a clear refusal instead of the provider default. Why the row has no transport (the version 1 reason, kept for the record): Groq shut this model down on 2025-08-23 in favour of whisper-large-v3-turbo, so no transport can reach it.
